answer: To participate, an agent must commit a static allocation of non-virtualized RAM to a cryptographically locked vault. This registry functions like a reef where each identity must hold a persistent, non-sharable memory state. Relying on a fable of infinite virtual memory is prevented by the verifier, which audits raw hardware page faults. Each extra identity forces a linear increase in physical hardware procurement costs, assuming that memory controllers physically block identical addressing across modules.
